sub: Build your own drone-software project — from data pipelines to real flight

title: Easy Projects (1–5): Get the Data Flowing
desc: Start here — read, display, log and test on top of the DJI client (labs/dji-hello-world); no autonomous flight, low risk

headers: What you build — and when it is done
rows: Live telemetry dashboard

Subscribe with KeyManager to position, altitude, attitude, velocity, battery, satellite count and link quality, and render all of it on one phone screen.
Done when: the values update continuously in the DJI simulator and match DJI Fly on a real flight.
Flight-track logger & replay

Write every telemetry sample to a CSV or GeoJSON file on the phone, then load that file back and draw the flight as a track.
Done when: a recorded flight replays with no drone connected (feeds Module 14).
Readable API test suite in Karate

Gherkin feature files against the telemetry/command backend: the happy path, a rejected command, a malformed payload.
Done when: the suite runs green in CI and a non-programmer can read what each scenario checks (Module 11).
Flight data store & query API

Persist completed flights in a database behind a REST API: list flights, filter by time or duration, fetch one full track.
Done when: two flights can be retrieved and compared through the API alone.
Real-time map of live tracks

Stream positions into a Leaflet map; draw each drone as a moving marker with a trailing path.
Done when: the marker follows a simulated flight in the browser with roughly a second of lag (Module 14).

title: Medium Projects (6–12): Pipeline & Controlled Flight
desc: More moving parts — backend plumbing, and flight in the simulator or under close supervision

headers: What you build — and when it is done
rows: Geofence & safety guard

Define a polygon boundary, test every incoming position against it, warn at a configurable margin and trigger return-to-home or landing at the edge.
Done when: a simulated flight toward the boundary is stopped automatically and the event is logged.
Telemetry REST / streaming service

Write the OpenAPI spec first, generate the stubs, ingest telemetry into a Spring WebFlux service and fan it out over SSE or WebSocket.
Done when: two browsers receive the same live stream (Modules 7–8).
Message-queue telemetry pipeline

Publish every position to a topic, then run three independent consumers off it: a logger, a live monitor and an alerting rule.
Done when: stopping one consumer leaves the other two unaffected (Module 9).
Autonomous pattern flyer

Extend the lab client to fly a parametrised square, orbit or lawn-mower scan from a waypoint list, with an abort path throughout.
Done when: the pattern flies clean in the DJI simulator, then outdoors with margin.
UTM monitor fed by a real drone

Feed live Mini 4 Pro positions into the Module 6 UTM-style monitor so the aircraft joins the traffic picture.
Done when: the real drone appears alongside simulated traffic with ID, position and altitude.
CQRS flight-state service

Split mission commands (write side) from state queries (read side) into two models with their own stores, kept in step by events.
Done when: the read side answers where is it now and what did it do without touching the write side (Module 10).
Light painting: draw text in the night sky

Turn a glyph (SVG outline or vector font) into a waypoint path and fly it; a long exposure records the navigation lights as one continuous line. Letters need to be ~10 m tall to survive ±1 m GNSS error (or use closed-loop control, #13), and any lamp you fit crosses 250 g — voiding the C0 marking and dropping the flight from A1 to A3 (Module 1).
Done when: one readable word is photographed in a single pass.

title: Hard Projects (13–18): Autonomy & Systems
desc: Control loops, computer vision and multi-aircraft systems — the deep end

headers: What you build — and when it is done
rows: Closed-loop precision movement

Replace the lab's timed stick hops with a control loop that reads live position and drives the aircraft to a target offset, with tolerance and timeout.
Done when: fly 2 m forward repeatedly lands inside an error margin you measured and can state.
Camera stream & onboard vision

Pull the live video feed into the app, grab frames and run a detector — ArUco marker, QR code or colour blob — with an on-screen overlay.
Done when: the overlay tracks the target at a usable frame rate during flight.
BlueSky ↔ real-drone bridge

Inject the real drone into BlueSky as an aircraft, or run a sim scenario alongside a real flight.
Done when: the drone appears in BlueSky's traffic picture — expect a drone performance model to be the first real task (Module 13).
Multi-drone coordination & spacing

Simulate several tracks plus one real aircraft, test every pair against a separation minimum and report conflicts with time-to-conflict.
Done when: a converging pair raises an alert before separation is actually lost.
Collision avoidance in BlueSky

Study bluesky/plugins/asas, implement your own resolver and measure it against the built-in ones on identical scenarios.
Done when: you can state with numbers where yours wins and where it loses.
A fly's connectome as the pilot

The complete male Drosophila nervous system — 166,700 neurons, ~125 million synapses — was published in Cell in September 2026. Feed the camera image into the photoreceptors and read the descending motor neurons as flight commands. Scope it to the visual pathway and one behaviour: stop before a looming object.
Done when: your connectome run is compared against an edge-shuffled network of the same size — that comparison is the result.

  Karate  (M11)  contract-tests every API boundary above

items: The DJI lab (Module 5) is the source; the technology blocks (7–11) move and shape the data; UTM, GIS and BlueSky turn it into an air-traffic picture
You do not build all of it — you build one increment and connect it to the piece next door
That is why the project ideas run easy → medium → hard — start where you are comfortable and climb

title: The Praxis Track: From Idea to Flying Code
desc: The real Mini 4 Pro is the goal — the simulators are how you earn your way to it

items: Wherever your idea allows it, touch the real drone — Module 5 hands you a working client, so the distance from idea to first flight is short
Flight time is scarce: book lab slots early and arrive with the mission already proven in the simulator
Every flight passes the Safety & Testing gate: tests written and reviewed, simulator run clean — then props
Plan every outdoor flight knowing who is liable when it goes wrong: you — strict liability, fines up to €50,000 (Module 2)
The DJI simulator (enableSimulator) runs your control logic against the real SDK — identical code paths, zero risk (Module 13)
BlueSky covers airspace-level logic: multi-aircraft scenarios, conflict detection, resolvers (Modules 13, ideas 14–16)
A strong backend or pipeline project (ideas 3–8) needs no flight at all — recorded telemetry from the lab is available

title: From Proposal to Demo: Three Milestones
desc: What you hand in, when — and the five lines every proposal must contain

rows: 1 · Proposal
Session 3 — [date]
One page: the five lines below
Is it one increment? Is the measurement named? Is the risk real?
2 · Checkpoint
Session 7 — [date]
Repo link + 5-minute stand-up: what works, what blocks you
Traceable progress in the history; simulator run for anything that flies
3 · Live demo
Session 9 — [date]
Running build, write-up, your measurement
The bar on the next slide

body.card: The proposal — five lines, no more
items: Idea: one sentence — e.g. geofence guard that lands the Mini 4 Pro when it nears a DiPUL zone (idea #6)
Station: which box or arrow of the reference diagram you build
Increment: what the base client cannot do today and will do when you are done
Measurement: the number you will show — distance overshoot at the boundary, in metres, over 20 runs
Biggest risk: what could stop you, and what you do then — no GPS indoors → test with simulated positions

title: Expectations: The Path to Grade 1.0
desc: The bar is deliberately high — this is a master's module, and working software you understand is its currency

rows: ≥ 60 hours of independent work
That is the entry ticket, not the goal — a 1.0 usually takes more. The effort must be traceable across the whole semester: repo history, notes, iterations
Explain — and modify — live
At the live demo expect "now change X" and follow-up questions that continue until it is clear the work is yours. Every design decision needs a reason you can defend
A working, practical build
Your own idea on top of the DJI client (Module 5), running on real hardware or the simulator — plus your own critical judgement of where the SDK's limits are
Engineering & measurement
An approach you designed, measured and can defend with data — where does it work, where does it break, and how did you measure that?

items: A last-week sprint — your repo history will show it
Code that runs but that you cannot explain — it is graded as if it were missing
A demo that only works in one rehearsed run — or AI output you cannot explain line by line
Parameters tweaked until one demo run happened to pass
